metadata.summary: This guideline addresses the assessment and management of women with suspected or confirmed endometriosis in Irish healthcare services. It covers clinical diagnosis, investigations, treatment of associated pain and infertility, and non-medical approaches to symptoms and well-being. Its recommendations are intended to support consistent care across primary, gynaecological and tertiary services while accounting for effects on quality of life and fertility.

target_population: women undergoing assessment or management of suspected or confirmed endometriosis

toxicities.event: Gastrointestinal adverse effects and potential kidney injury

prevention: Opioid medication is not recommended for endometriosis-associated pain because of adverse effects and the potential for dependency.

toxicities.event: Severe adverse effects associated with danazol
prevention: Danazol is no longer recommended for endometriosis because similarly effective medical options are available without its severe adverse-effect profile.

toxicities.event: Menopausal symptoms and other adverse effects during GnRH agonist treatment
prevention: Add-back hormonal treatment is recommended alongside GnRH agonists to counter adverse effects. Studies comparing intramuscular, subcutaneous and intranasal administration reported no difference in hot flushes, vaginal dryness, headaches or decreased libido.

toxicities.event: Loss of bone mineral density during GnRH agonist treatment
recognition: Reduced bone mineral density with long-term treatment
prevention: Prescribe add-back hormonal treatment with GnRH agonists to prevent bone loss. In the Cochrane review by Veth et al., higher GnRH agonist doses appeared associated with greater bone mineral density loss; the review found no certain effect of dose on pain.

toxicities.incidence: More than 70% of women in each trial group reported at least one adverse event; adverse events were significantly more frequent with the higher dose of elagolix than with placebo.

toxicities.event: Hot flushes and bone mineral density reduction during relugolix treatment
toxicities.incidence: In the SPIRIT 1 and 2 trials, mean bone mineral density reduction after 24 weeks of combination relugolix + HRT was less that 1% and was not considered clinically significant. Participants whose HRT began only after 12 weeks of relugolix monotherapy were more likely to have hot flushes and substantial bone density reduction.
prevention: The SPIRIT 1 and 2 findings suggest that combining relugolix with HRT from the start retains efficacy while reducing adverse-event risk compared with delayed HRT. For the relugolix combination formulation available in Ireland, bone densitometry is recommended after 1 year of treatment and thereafter when considered appropriate.

toxicities.event: Adverse effects associated with aromatase inhibitors
prevention: Because of these severe adverse effects, aromatase inhibitors should be prescribed only after other medical and surgical options have been exhausted. Evidence on their long-term effects is lacking.

toxicities.event: Ovarian injury or reduced ovarian reserve after endometrioma surgery
toxicities.incidence: The reported risk of ovarian failure after surgery for bilateral endometriomata is 2.4%.
prevention: Use caution to limit ovarian damage, particularly with recurrent endometrioma or concern about ovarian reserve. Meta-analyses found non-thermal haemostasis, using suture or haemostatic agents, preferable to diathermy according to postoperative AMH levels. Before surgery, discuss reduced ovarian reserve and possible ovarian loss; for bilateral endometriomas, discuss the possibility of freezing oocytes beforehand.

toxicities.event: Complications after laparoscopic excision of rectovaginal endometriosis
toxicities.incidence: In a study of almost 5000 women, overall complications occurred in 6.8% of operations; major gastrointestinal complications occurred in 1.1% of operations, and urinary tract complications occurred in 1% of procedures.
recognition: Ureteric or bladder injury or leak
prevention: Discuss expected benefits and surgical risks as part of informed consent. The guideline prefers surgery for severe deep disease by an experienced surgeon in a multidisciplinary setting using a minimally invasive approach.

toxicities.event: Postoperative complications of bowel endometriosis surgery
toxicities.incidence: Postoperative complications have been reported in up to 13.9% of cases.

toxicities.event: Persistent or recurrent pain after hysterectomy for endometriosis
toxicities.incidence: Hysterectomy with ovarian conservation was reported to carry a 6-fold risk of recurrent pain and an 8.1-times greater risk of reoperation.
recognition: Endometriosis symptoms may persist after hysterectomy
prevention: Advise women that hysterectomy does not always relieve endometriosis symptoms. If hysterectomy is performed, excise all visible endometriosis lesions; the guideline recommends total rather than sub-total hysterectomy because endometriosis may persist in or near a retained cervix.
If oophorectomy is under consideration, discuss the consequences of early menopause and the possible need for MHT.

toxicities.event: Possible recurrence of endometriosis during MHT after surgical menopause
prevention: A systematic review limited to two RCTs found a small association between MHT and endometriosis recurrence. If MHT is needed in someone with a history of endometriosis, the guideline advises a continuous oestrogen-progestogen regimen.

prophylaxis.recommendation: Prescribe add-back hormonal treatment when prescribing GnRH agonists to prevent bone loss and counter treatment-related menopausal symptoms.
prophylaxis.target_population: Women receiving GnRH agonists for endometriosis-associated pain

prophylaxis.recommendation: Consider hormonal suppression after endometriosis surgery to reduce recurrence of endometriosis-associated pain.
prophylaxis.target_population: Women who do not plan to conceive immediately after endometriosis surgery

prophylaxis.recommendation: Use nonhormonal contraception when starting the relugolix combination formulation.
prophylaxis.duration: at least the first month of treatment

prophylaxis.recommendation: Take precautions to minimise ovarian damage during surgery for endometrioma. Discuss possible preoperative oocyte freezing when endometriomas are bilateral.
prophylaxis.target_population: Women undergoing endometrioma surgery, particularly those with recurrent or bilateral endometriomas or concern about ovarian reserve

infection_management.pathogen_or_syndrome: Urinary tract infection after surgical treatment of bowel endometriosis
Abdominal wall abscess after surgical treatment of bowel endometriosis

conditions.name: endometriosis
conditions.description: A chronic, oestrogen-mediated inflammatory condition of uncertain cause in which tissue resembling endometrium occurs outside the uterus. Lesions commonly affect pelvic structures but may also occur outside the pelvis or be found incidentally during laparoscopy.
conditions.epidemiology: The guideline estimates that endometriosis affects 1 in 10 women and cites a World Health Organization estimate of 190 million women affected worldwide. Symptoms can begin in young women and persist after menopause. The reported average interval from symptom onset to confirmed diagnosis is 7-8 years.
conditions.clinical_presentation: Presentations vary widely and do not reliably reflect the apparent extent of disease. Possible features include chronic pelvic pain, dysmenorrhoea that disrupts daily activities, deep dyspareunia, cyclical bowel symptoms—particularly dyschezia—cyclical urinary symptoms, and infertility. Fatigue, cyclical cough, haemoptysis, chest pain, pneumothorax, shoulder tip pain and scar swelling may also occur. Some women have no symptoms. Symptoms overlap with those of bowel and bladder disorders, musculoskeletal pain conditions and fibromyalgia.

subtypes.name: superficial peritoneal endometriosis
subtypes.distinguishing_features: Peritoneal disease may be missed on imaging, particularly when imaging findings are negative.

subtypes.name: ovarian endometrioma
subtypes.distinguishing_features: Ovarian disease that can be identified reliably with TVUS or MRI; other forms of endometriosis may coexist.

subtypes.name: deeply infiltrative endometriosis
subtypes.distinguishing_features: Disease extending beneath the peritoneum that may affect the uterosacral ligaments, pelvic side walls, rectovaginal septum, vagina, bowel, bladder or ureters.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Identify symptoms suggestive of endometriosis and support a presumptive diagnosis.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: When endometriosis is suspected.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: A combination of symptoms, especially when cyclical, increases the likelihood of endometriosis; no symptom is specific to the disease.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess organ mobility, tenderness, posterior vaginal nodules and pelvic or abdominal masses.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Offer when symptoms suggest endometriosis; perform pelvic examination where appropriate.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: A normal examination does not exclude endometriosis, and examination alone cannot establish the diagnosis reliably.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Look for visible vaginal endometriotic lesions.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Where appropriate during clinical examination.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess possible rectosigmoid infiltration or nodules and adnexal masses.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Consider where appropriate, with explicit consent and recognition that it may cause discomfort.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Investigate suspected endometriosis, particularly ovarian endometrioma or deeply infiltrative disease.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Offer as part of the investigation of suspected endometriosis.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Negative imaging does not exclude endometriosis, particularly superficial peritoneal disease. In the Nisenblat et al. review, TVUS had 95% specificity and 65% sensitivity for superficial pelvic disease, 94% specificity and 79% sensitivity for deeply infiltrative disease, and 96% specificity and 95% sensitivity for ovarian endometriomas.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Provide an alternative ultrasound approach.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Consider if transvaginal ultrasound is inappropriate or not tolerated.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess the presence and extent of suspected deeply infiltrative lesions, including disease affecting the bowel, bladder or ureter.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Recommended for suspected deeply infiltrative disease involving the bowel, bladder or ureter; not recommended as the first-line diagnostic investigation.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Negative imaging does not exclude endometriosis. The cited evidence reports 91% specificity and 95% sensitivity for endometriomas, and 72% specificity and 79% sensitivity for superficial peritoneal lesions.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: The guideline discusses these imaging methods in relation to diagnosis; CT may have a role in planning surgery for deep disease involving the bladder, ureters and/or bowel.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Neither CT nor PET-CT is recommended to diagnose endometriosis.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: The evidence for diagnostic use is limited.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: The guideline evaluates, but does not recommend, its use for diagnosing endometriosis.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Do not use to diagnose endometriosis.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: An incidental result >35 IU/ml may be consistent with endometriosis, but disease can be present despite a result <35 IU/ml. A cited review reported pooled specificity 93% and sensitivity 52%; a negative result cannot rule out disease.

diagnostic_workup.test: Other endometrial, urinary and blood biomarkers
diagnostic_workup.purpose: Investigated as possible diagnostic tests.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Diagnostic biomarkers are not recommended.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: The cited systematic reviews found no biomarker suitable to replace laparoscopy for diagnosis.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Inspect the pelvis and abdomen for lesions, enable biopsy and provide an opportunity to classify disease.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Consider if empirical treatment is ineffective or inappropriate, including when imaging is negative.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: A negative result after thorough assessment has high negative predictive value, whereas an incomplete assessment can produce a false-negative result.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Confirm lesions suspected at laparoscopy; histology can also help exclude ovarian malignancy when an endometrioma is sampled or removed.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Take a biopsy of suspected lesions during diagnostic laparoscopy.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Negative histology does not entirely exclude endometriosis.

staging.additional_rules: The guideline reports no agreed gold-standard classification. It describes rASRM as widely used but poorly reproducible, weakly correlated with pain and not inclusive of deep lesions in several organs. ENZIAN addresses deep and retroperitoneal disease and can be calculated from imaging for preoperative planning, but is not widely used and needs further evaluation for imaging-based application. AAGL can use imaging or operative findings, relates stages to surgical complexity and has not been fully validated. The guideline cites a proposed surgical classification toolbox using rASRM with ENZIAN and EFI where applicable.

prognostic_tools.name: EFI
prognostic_tools.interpretation: Predicts the likelihood of pregnancy following surgery for endometriosis and may help identify women who could benefit from ART. The guideline also describes its use when assessing prospects for natural or IUI conception.

long_term_effects: Persistent pain may contribute to central sensitisation.
Symptoms relapse after surgical treatment in 40-45% of women, and up to 30% undergo another procedure within five years of their first surgery.
follow_up.survivorship_notes: Endometriosis-related pain may disrupt daily life, work, mental and physical wellbeing, relationships and fertility. Symptom-free women do not necessarily need treatment.

conditions.name: superficial peritoneal endometriosis
conditions.description: A peritoneal form of endometriosis for which negative imaging is particularly unreliable as evidence of absence.
conditions.clinical_presentation: The observed extent of disease may not correspond to pain severity; minimal apparent disease can coexist with severe symptoms.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Investigate suspected endometriosis.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Offer during the investigation of suspected disease.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: The Nisenblat et al. review reported 95% specificity and 65% sensitivity for superficial pelvic endometriosis. A negative result does not exclude superficial peritoneal disease.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess suspected endometriosis where imaging is used.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Not recommended as the first-line diagnostic test.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: The guideline reports limited value for superficial peritoneal lesions, with 72% specificity and 79% sensitivity; a negative result does not exclude disease.

diagnostic_workup.test: Laparoscopy with biopsy and histological examination
diagnostic_workup.purpose: Inspect for lesions and obtain histological confirmation.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Consider when suggestive symptoms persist and empirical treatment is ineffective or inappropriate, even after negative imaging.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Negative histology does not completely rule out endometriosis. A thorough laparoscopic assessment is important because an incomplete examination can give a false-negative result.

staging.additional_rules: The guideline does not provide stage definitions and notes poor correlation between rASRM stage and pain symptoms.

conditions.name: ovarian endometrioma
conditions.description: An ovarian manifestation of endometriosis that can occur alongside other disease, including deeply infiltrative endometriosis.
conditions.epidemiology: In a cited study of 1,191 women undergoing ultrasound during infertility investigation, 56% (n=70) of women with endometrioma also had DIE lesions.
conditions.clinical_presentation: May occur with pain or infertility. Other forms of endometriosis should be anticipated when operating on a woman with an endometrioma and pain.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Detect an ovarian endometrioma and assess for coexisting disease.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: During investigation of suspected endometriosis.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: The Nisenblat et al. review reported 96% specificity and 95% sensitivity for detecting ovarian endometriomas.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Identify an endometrioma and assess disease where imaging is indicated.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Not recommended as the first-line diagnostic test for endometriosis.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: The guideline reports 91% specificity and 95% sensitivity for diagnosing endometriomas.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Substantiate a visible lesion and help exclude ovarian malignancy.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: When an endometrioma is drained, sampled or surgically excised.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: A negative histological result does not rule out endometriosis.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess ovarian reserve.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: A cited narrative review suggests serial assessment during expectant management of an asymptomatic endometrioma; ovarian reserve is also a consideration when planning surgery for infertility.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Monitor an endometrioma managed expectantly.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Suggested for serial assessment by a cited narrative review of asymptomatic endometriomas.

staging.additional_rules: The guideline provides no stage definitions for ovarian endometrioma.

prognostic_tools.name: EFI
prognostic_tools.interpretation: May inform the chance of conception after surgery for endometriosis and decisions about ART.

recommended_tests: Serial cyst size assessment and AMH or antral follicle count are suggested by a cited narrative review for expectantly managed asymptomatic endometriomas.
long_term_effects: Surgery may reduce ovarian reserve; the guideline reports a 2.4% risk of ovarian failure after surgery for bilateral endometriomata.
follow_up.survivorship_notes: The guideline advises particular care when considering surgery for recurrent or bilateral endometriomas because of its potential effect on ovarian reserve.

conditions.name: deeply infiltrative endometriosis
conditions.description: Endometriosis extending beneath the peritoneum that can involve pelvic side walls, uterosacral ligaments, the rectovaginal septum, vagina, bowel, bladder or ureters and impair the function of affected organs.
conditions.epidemiology: The guideline reports bowel involvement in 5-12% of women affected by endometriosis.
conditions.clinical_presentation: May cause endometriosis-associated pain or infertility. Findings can include reduced organ mobility or vaginal nodules; manifestations depend on the organs involved.

subtypes.name: bowel endometriosis
subtypes.distinguishing_features: May cause altered bowel habit, constipation, diarrhoea, tenesmus, dyschezia or rectal bleeding. The guideline states that almost 90% of bowel cases involve the sigmoid colon or rectum.

subtypes.name: bladder endometriosis
subtypes.distinguishing_features: Bladder involvement can be associated with cyclical urinary symptoms, particularly dysuria and/or haematuria.

subtypes.name: ureteric endometriosis
subtypes.distinguishing_features: Women typically do not report specific urinary tract symptoms, according to a cited review.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess reduced mobility, vaginal or uterosacral nodules, pouch of Douglas infiltration and visible vaginal lesions.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: When symptoms suggest endometriosis and examination is appropriate.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: A normal examination does not exclude endometriosis.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess possible rectosigmoid infiltration or a mass.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Consider with explicit consent and recognition of possible discomfort.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Identify deep disease, including possible bowel, bladder or ureter involvement.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: As part of investigation for suspected endometriosis.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: The Nisenblat et al. review reported 94% specificity and 79% sensitivity for deeply infiltrative disease; sensitivity reached up to 87% when 3-D ultrasound was used. A negative finding does not exclude disease.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Determine the presence and extent of deep lesions for assessment and planning.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Recommended when bowel, bladder or ureter involvement is suspected.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: For rectosigmoid lesions, the guideline cites up to 91% sensitivity and 96% specificity for estimating invasion.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Potentially assist operative planning for deep lesions involving the bladder, ureters and/or bowel.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Not recommended for diagnosing endometriosis.

diagnostic_workup.test: Laparoscopy with biopsy and histological examination
diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess abdominal and pelvic disease and confirm suspected lesions histologically.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Consider when empirical treatment is ineffective or inappropriate, even if imaging is negative.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Negative histology does not entirely rule out endometriosis.

staging.additional_rules: ENZIAN includes deep and retroperitoneal structures and can be calculated using imaging for preoperative planning. The guideline notes that rASRM omits deep involvement of the uterosacral ligaments, bladder, vagina and bowel. No stage definitions are provided.

prognostic_tools.name: EFI
prognostic_tools.interpretation: The cited classification toolbox includes EFI where infertility is relevant; it estimates the chance of pregnancy after endometriosis surgery.

long_term_effects: In a cited study of 135 women with moderate or severe deeply infiltrative disease managed expectantly for a median of 666 days, ultrasound findings progressed in 37%, regressed in 13% and remained static in 50%.
follow_up.survivorship_notes: Suspected or confirmed disease affecting the bowel, bladder or ureter warrants referral to a specialist endometriosis service.

conditions.name: bowel endometriosis
conditions.description: Deep endometriosis affecting the bowel, most commonly the sigmoid colon or rectum.
conditions.epidemiology: Bowel disease is reported in 5-12% of women with endometriosis; almost 90% of bowel cases involve the sigmoid colon or rectum.
conditions.clinical_presentation: Possible features include altered bowel habit, constipation, diarrhoea, tenesmus, dyschezia and rectal bleeding. Bowel symptoms may be cyclical.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess deep nodules or rectosigmoid infiltration.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Where appropriate; rectovaginal examination requires explicit consent and recognition of possible discomfort.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: A normal examination does not exclude endometriosis.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess suspected deeply infiltrative bowel disease.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: As part of investigation for suspected endometriosis.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: A negative finding does not exclude endometriosis.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess bowel lesions and their extent, including depth and length of rectosigmoid invasion.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Recommended when deep bowel involvement is suspected.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: The guideline cites up to 91% sensitivity and 96% specificity for rectosigmoid lesions.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: May contribute to surgical planning for deeply infiltrative bowel disease.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Not recommended to diagnose endometriosis.

diagnostic_workup.test: Laparoscopy with biopsy and histological examination
diagnostic_workup.purpose: Inspect and obtain histological confirmation of suspected lesions.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Consider when empirical treatment is ineffective or inappropriate, including after negative imaging.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Negative histology does not entirely exclude endometriosis.

staging.additional_rules: ENZIAN addresses deep disease that rASRM does not include; the guideline gives no bowel-specific stage definitions.

follow_up.survivorship_notes: Suspected or confirmed bowel involvement warrants referral to a specialist endometriosis service.

conditions.name: bladder endometriosis
conditions.description: Endometriosis involving the bladder as a form of deeply infiltrative disease.
conditions.clinical_presentation: Cyclical urinary symptoms, particularly dysuria and/or haematuria, can raise suspicion of urinary tract endometriosis.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess possible deeply infiltrative bladder involvement.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: As part of investigation for suspected endometriosis.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Negative imaging does not exclude endometriosis.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess the presence and extent of suspected deep bladder lesions.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Recommended when deeply infiltrative bladder disease is suspected.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: May assist planning surgery for deep bladder disease.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Not recommended for diagnosis of endometriosis.

diagnostic_workup.test: Laparoscopy with biopsy and histological examination
diagnostic_workup.purpose: Inspect and obtain histological confirmation of suspected lesions.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Consider if empirical treatment is ineffective or inappropriate, even after negative imaging.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Negative histology does not entirely exclude endometriosis.

staging.additional_rules: The guideline notes that rASRM does not include deep bladder involvement and supplies no bladder-specific stage definitions.

follow_up.survivorship_notes: Suspected or confirmed bladder involvement warrants referral to a specialist endometriosis service.

conditions.name: ureteric endometriosis
conditions.description: Deeply infiltrative endometriosis involving a ureter; lesions may be associated with obstruction.
conditions.epidemiology: In a cited systematic review of 700 women with ureteric endometriosis, the left ureter was affected in 53.6%, bilateral disease occurred in 10.6%, and bladder and ureteric disease coexisted in 19.8%.
conditions.clinical_presentation: According to the cited review, women typically did not report specific urinary tract symptoms.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess possible deeply infiltrative ureteric disease.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: As part of investigation for suspected endometriosis.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Negative imaging does not exclude endometriosis.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess the presence and extent of suspected deep ureteric lesions.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Recommended when ureteric involvement is suspected.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: May assist surgical planning for deep ureteric involvement.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Not recommended for diagnosing endometriosis.

diagnostic_workup.test: Laparoscopy with biopsy and histological examination
diagnostic_workup.purpose: Inspect suspected lesions and obtain histological confirmation.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Consider if empirical treatment is ineffective or inappropriate, even when imaging is negative.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Negative histology does not entirely rule out endometriosis.

staging.additional_rules: ENZIAN addresses deep and retroperitoneal disease; the guideline provides no ureter-specific stage definitions.

follow_up.survivorship_notes: Suspected or confirmed ureteric involvement warrants referral to a specialist endometriosis service.

conditions.name: endometriosis-associated infertility
conditions.description: Difficulty conceiving in the setting of endometriosis; it may be present with or without pain.
conditions.epidemiology: The guideline reports endometriosis in 35-50% of women presenting with infertility.
conditions.clinical_presentation: A woman may initially present with infertility alone or alongside endometriosis-associated pain.

diagnostic_workup.test: Assessment of endometriosis stage and disease type
diagnostic_workup.purpose: Characterise peritoneal, ovarian and/or deeply infiltrative disease when planning fertility care.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: During evaluation of endometriosis-associated infertility.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: The potential effect of surgery on spontaneous conception depends on disease stage or type.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Inform fertility evaluation and decisions about surgery, particularly for recurrent or bilateral endometrioma.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: During fertility workup and when surgery is considered.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess the partner’s fertility contribution and inform shared surgical decisions.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: During fertility workup.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Investigate suspected endometriosis, including endometrioma or deeply infiltrative disease.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: As part of investigation for suspected endometriosis.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Negative imaging does not exclude endometriosis.

diagnostic_workup.test: Laparoscopy with biopsy and histological examination
diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess and confirm suspected endometriosis and provide findings relevant to staging.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Consider when empirical treatment is inappropriate or ineffective, including in women trying to conceive.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Negative histology does not entirely rule out endometriosis.

staging.additional_rules: The guideline distinguishes stage I-II from stage III-IV when discussing fertility outcomes and management but does not define those stages. It cites a proposed classification toolbox incorporating EFI for infertility where applicable.

prognostic_tools.name: EFI
prognostic_tools.interpretation: Estimates the likelihood of natural or IUI conception after endometriosis surgery and may help identify women who could benefit from ART. The guideline describes it as validated in a meta-analysis of over 30 studies.

follow_up.survivorship_notes: The guideline notes limited evidence about live birth outcomes for several approaches to endometriosis-associated infertility.

recommendations.statement: Consider endometriosis when a woman has at least one of these symptoms: chronic pelvic pain; dysmenorrhoea that disrupts daily activities; deep dyspareunia; cyclical bowel symptoms, particularly dyschezia; cyclical urinary symptoms, particularly dysuria and/or haematuria; or infertility.
recommendations.source_heading: Key Recommendations — Diagnosis of endometriosis

recommendations.statement: Offer abdominal and pelvic examination when symptoms suggest endometriosis, assessing for reduced organ mobility, tender nodules in the posterior vagina, and pelvic or abdominal masses.
recommendations.source_heading: Key Recommendations — Diagnosis of endometriosis

recommendations.statement: Do not delay discussing and starting empirical treatment in women with suspected endometriosis.
recommendations.rationale: Treatment may improve quality of life.
recommendations.source_heading: Key Recommendations — Diagnosis of endometriosis

recommendations.statement: Refer women with suspected or confirmed endometriosis to a Gynaecologist if symptoms are severe, persistent or recurrent; examination reveals signs of endometriosis; infertility is present; initial management is ineffective, intolerable or contraindicated; or imaging suggests higher-stage or deeply infiltrating disease, such as endometrioma or invasion of another organ.
recommendations.source_heading: Key Recommendations — Diagnosis of endometriosis

recommendations.statement: Refer women with suspected or confirmed deeply infiltrative endometriosis affecting the bowel, bladder or ureter to a specialist endometriosis service.
recommendations.source_heading: Key Recommendations — Diagnosis of endometriosis

recommendations.statement: Offer transvaginal ultrasound when investigating suspected endometriosis; consider a transabdominal approach when transvaginal ultrasound is inappropriate.
recommendations.source_heading: Key Recommendations — Diagnosis of endometriosis

recommendations.statement: Do not use MRI as the first-line investigation for endometriosis; use it when deeply infiltrative endometriosis involving the bowel, bladder or ureter is suspected.
recommendations.source_heading: Key Recommendations — Diagnosis of endometriosis

recommendations.statement: Do not use computed tomography (CT) or positron emission tomography-CT (PET-CT) to diagnose endometriosis.
recommendations.source_heading: Key Recommendations — Diagnosis of endometriosis

recommendations.statement: Do not rule out endometriosis because imaging findings are negative.
recommendations.source_heading: Key Recommendations — Diagnosis of endometriosis

recommendations.statement: Do not use biomarkers, including serum CA-125, to diagnose endometriosis.
recommendations.source_heading: Key Recommendations — Diagnosis of endometriosis

recommendations.statement: Consider laparoscopy for women whose symptoms suggest endometriosis when empirical treatment is ineffective or inappropriate, even if imaging is negative.
recommendations.source_heading: Key Recommendations — Diagnosis of endometriosis

recommendations.statement: During laparoscopy, biopsy lesions suspected to be endometriosis for histological confirmation; recognise that negative histology does not completely exclude endometriosis.
recommendations.source_heading: Key Recommendations — Diagnosis of endometriosis

recommendations.statement: Refer for laparoscopy to a Gynaecologist with suitable laparoscopic training and skills to optimise assessment of the pelvis and abdomen.
recommendations.source_heading: Key Recommendations — Diagnosis of endometriosis

recommendations.statement: Offer analgesics, including paracetamol, nonsteroidal anti-inflammatories and neuromodulator therapies, to reduce endometriosis-associated pain.
recommendations.source_heading: Key Recommendations — Treatment of endometriosis-associated pain

recommendations.statement: Offer combined hormonal contraception or progestogens as first-line hormonal treatment for endometriosis-associated pain.
recommendations.source_heading: Key Recommendations — Treatment of endometriosis-associated pain

recommendations.statement: Offer GnRH agonists or antagonists together with add-back hormone replacement therapy as second-line treatment for endometriosis-associated pain.
recommendations.source_heading: Key Recommendations — Treatment of endometriosis-associated pain

recommendations.statement: Make treatment decisions jointly with the woman, taking account of her wish to conceive and each medication’s side-effect profile, cost and availability.
recommendations.source_heading: Key Recommendations — Treatment of endometriosis-associated pain

recommendations.statement: Consider hormonal suppression after endometriosis surgery if the woman does not intend to conceive immediately.
recommendations.source_heading: Key Recommendations — Treatment of endometriosis-associated pain

recommendations.statement: Offer surgery as an option for reducing endometriosis-associated pain.
recommendations.source_heading: Key Recommendations — Treatment of endometriosis-associated pain

recommendations.statement: When choosing hormonal or surgical treatment for endometriosis-related pain, use shared decision-making that considers the woman’s preferences, adverse effects, individual effectiveness, costs and treatment availability.
recommendations.source_heading: Key Recommendations — Treatment of endometriosis-associated pain

recommendations.statement: If surgery is undertaken for endometriosis-associated pain, clinicians may consider excising rather than ablating endometriosis.
recommendations.source_heading: Key Recommendations — Treatment of endometriosis-associated pain

recommendations.statement: When operating on a woman with an endometrioma and pain, anticipate that other endometriosis, including deeply infiltrative endometriosis, may commonly be found.
recommendations.source_heading: Key Recommendations — Treatment of endometriosis-associated pain

recommendations.statement: Use cystectomy or CO2 laser vaporisation rather than drainage and coagulation for ovarian endometrioma, while taking care to minimise ovarian damage.
recommendations.rationale: Cystectomy or CO2 laser vaporisation can lower recurrence of endometrioma and endometriosis-associated pain.
recommendations.source_heading: Key Recommendations — Treatment of endometriosis-associated pain

recommendations.statement: Surgical removal of deeply infiltrative endometriosis may lessen endometriosis-associated pain and improve quality of life.
recommendations.source_heading: Key Recommendations — Treatment of endometriosis-associated pain

recommendations.statement: Have deeply infiltrative endometriosis removed by a surgeon experienced in deep-disease surgery, preferably within a multidisciplinary service using a minimally invasive approach intended to remove all endometriosis lesions.
recommendations.source_heading: Key Recommendations — Treatment of endometriosis-associated pain

recommendations.statement: Consider hysterectomy, with or without oophorectomy, for women who do not intend to conceive and have not benefited from conservative treatment; explain that hysterectomy does not invariably resolve endometriosis symptoms.
recommendations.source_heading: Key Recommendations — Treatment of endometriosis-associated pain

recommendations.statement: Perform total rather than sub-total hysterectomy.
recommendations.rationale: With sub-total hysterectomy, endometriosis may persist within or beside the retained cervix.
recommendations.source_heading: Key Recommendations — Treatment of endometriosis-associated pain

recommendations.statement: If considering oophorectomy, discuss the consequences of early menopause and the possible need for menopausal hormone therapy (MHT).
recommendations.source_heading: Key Recommendations — Treatment of endometriosis-associated pain

recommendations.statement: If MHT is needed by a woman with a history of endometriosis, use a continuous oestrogen-progestogen regimen.
recommendations.source_heading: Key Recommendations — Treatment of endometriosis-associated pain

recommendations.statement: Do not prescribe hormonal suppression to women with endometriosis-associated infertility who are attempting to conceive.
recommendations.source_heading: Key Recommendations — Treatment of endometriosis-associated infertility

recommendations.statement: When considering surgery for endometriosis-associated infertility, account for the woman’s age, ovarian reserve, duration of infertility and other fertility factors.
recommendations.source_heading: Key Recommendations — Treatment of endometriosis-associated infertility

recommendations.statement: Offer operative laparoscopy to women with stage I-II endometriosis and associated infertility.
recommendations.rationale: Operative laparoscopy improves the likelihood of an ongoing clinical pregnancy.
recommendations.source_heading: Key Recommendations — Treatment of endometriosis-associated infertility

recommendations.statement: Clinicians may consider operative laparoscopy for endometrioma with associated infertility. Decide jointly with the woman after considering ovarian reserve, prior surgery, symptoms, other fertility investigation results and any planned fertility treatment.
recommendations.rationale: Surgery may increase the likelihood of spontaneous pregnancy.
recommendations.source_heading: Key Recommendations — Treatment of endometriosis-associated infertility

recommendations.statement: Do not routinely operate on an endometrioma before assisted reproductive technology (ART); surgery may be considered to address pain or improve access to follicles.
recommendations.source_heading: Key Recommendations — Treatment of endometriosis-associated infertility

recommendations.statement: Consider operative laparoscopy as an option for women with deeply infiltrative endometriosis and infertility, guided by pain symptoms and the woman’s preference.
recommendations.source_heading: Key Recommendations — Treatment of endometriosis-associated infertility

recommendations.statement: Consider intra-uterine insemination (IUI) with ovarian stimulation for infertility associated with stage I-II endometriosis.
recommendations.source_heading: Key Recommendations — Treatment of endometriosis-associated infertility

recommendations.statement: Use ART to treat endometriosis-associated infertility, particularly when tubal function is impaired or male factor infertility coexists.
recommendations.source_heading: Key Recommendations — Treatment of endometriosis-associated infertility

recommendations.statement: Although no recommendation can be made for any individual non-medical intervention—traditional Chinese medicine, nutrition, electrotherapy, acupuncture, physiotherapy or psychological interventions—to treat endometriosis-related symptoms, clinicians may discuss these approaches with women in relation to quality of life and psychological well-being.
recommendations.rationale: Evidence does not support a recommendation for any individual intervention.
recommendations.source_heading: Key Recommendations — Role of non-medical interventions for the treatment of endometriosis

therapies_index.name: paracetamol
approved_indications: Relief of endometriosis-associated pain, including cyclical or menstrual pain; may be used with NSAIDs.

therapies_index.name: NSAIDs
approved_indications: Relief of endometriosis-associated pain, alone or with paracetamol.
key_toxicities: Undesirable gastrointestinal effects with long-term use
Potential kidney injury with long-term use

therapies_index.name: co-proxamol
therapies_index.administration: The cited formulation contained paracetamol 650 mg and dextropropoxyphene 65 mg; no dosing schedule is given. Removed from the Irish market in 2007 and available only on a named-patient basis.
key_toxicities: Safety concerns prompted its removal from the Irish market; specific adverse effects are not identified.

therapies_index.name: neuromodulator therapies
therapies_index.mechanism: Act as mediators of pain within the central nervous system.
approved_indications: May be used for endometriosis-associated pain, generally within a broader strategy involving a specialist pain management service.
therapies_index.administration: May be combined with oral contraceptive medications, progestogens, and GnRH agonists and antagonists.
key_toxicities: Sometimes associated with severe, dose-limiting adverse effects

therapies_index.name: combined hormonal contraception
approved_indications: First-line treatment of endometriosis-associated pain; also used after surgery to prolong pain reduction when immediate conception is not planned.
therapies_index.administration: Options described are an oral pill, vaginal ring or transdermal patch.

therapies_index.name: COCP
approved_indications: First-line hormonal treatment to reduce endometriosis-associated pain.
therapies_index.administration: The guideline recommends continuous rather than cyclic use.

therapies_index.name: ethinylestradiol (EE) 15 mg + etonogestrel 120 mg/d
approved_indications: Investigated in a patient-preference trial for endometriosis-associated pain; the trial found the vaginal ring more effective than the transdermal patch studied.
therapies_index.administration: Vaginal ring used continuously for 48-week treatment in the cited trial.

therapies_index.name: EE 20 mg + norelgestromin 150 mg/d
approved_indications: Investigated as a transdermal comparator for endometriosis-associated pain in a patient-preference trial.
therapies_index.administration: Transdermal patch in the cited trial.

therapies_index.name: progestogens
approved_indications: First-line treatment of endometriosis-associated pain; also offered after surgery to prolong pain reduction when immediate conception is not planned.
therapies_index.administration: Described options include an oral pill, levonorgestrel intrauterine system, etonogestrel-releasing implant and medroxyprogesterone acetate depot injection.

therapies_index.name: LNG-IUS
approved_indications: May be offered to reduce endometriosis-associated pain; evidence supporting its use specifically to prevent symptomatic recurrence after surgery is not high quality.
therapies_index.administration: Intrauterine system.

therapies_index.name: levonorgestrel
therapies_index.administration: An intrauterine system is described.

therapies_index.name: etonogestrel-releasing subdermal implant
approved_indications: May be offered to reduce endometriosis-associated pain.
therapies_index.administration: Subdermal implant.

therapies_index.name: etonogestrel
therapies_index.administration: Described in a subdermal implant and in a vaginal-ring combination.

therapies_index.name: medroxyprogesterone acetate
approved_indications: A depot injection is listed among options for endometriosis-associated pain.
therapies_index.administration: Depot intramuscular injection is described.

therapies_index.name: GnRH agonists
approved_indications: Second-line treatment of endometriosis-associated pain, with add-back hormone replacement therapy.
therapies_index.administration: Intramuscular, subcutaneous and intranasal administration are described; the guideline identifies no agreed specific dose or treatment duration.
key_toxicities: Loss of bone mineral density with long-term treatment

therapies_index.name: GnRH antagonists
approved_indications: Second-line treatment of endometriosis-associated pain, with add-back hormone replacement therapy.
therapies_index.administration: The guideline identifies no agreed dose or treatment duration for the class.

therapies_index.name: elagolix
approved_indications: Reduced endometriosis-associated pain versus placebo in the cited trials.
therapies_index.administration: Oral treatment was studied at two different doses; the doses are not specified.

therapies_index.name: linzagolix
approved_indications: Its efficacy for endometriosis-associated pain is supported by a small randomised trial cited in the guideline.

therapies_index.name: relugolix
approved_indications: The guideline states that a combination formulation containing relugolix is licensed for endometriosis in Ireland.
therapies_index.administration: Studied as oral monotherapy and with add-back HRT; the guideline does not give a monotherapy dose.
key_toxicities: In the delayed-add-back trial arm, hot flushes and substantial bone-density reduction were more likely than with combination treatment from the outset.

therapies_index.name: 40 mg relugolix/1 mg estradiol hemihydrate/0.5 mg norethisterone
approved_indications: Licensed in Ireland for endometriosis; the guideline notes that it was not reimbursed by the HSE at publication.
therapies_index.administration: One tablet daily. Nonhormonal contraception is required for at least the first month of treatment.
key_toxicities: In the cited combination-treatment study, mean bone mineral density fell by less that 1% after 24 weeks; this was not considered clinically significant.
monitoring: Bone densitometry after 1 year of treatment and subsequently when considered appropriate.

therapies_index.name: norethisterone/norethindrone acetate (NETA)
approved_indications: Described as a progestogen-only add-back option during GnRH agonist treatment.

therapies_index.name: add-back hormone replacement therapy
approved_indications: Recommended alongside second-line GnRH agonists or antagonists for endometriosis-associated pain; add-back treatment with GnRH agonists is used to limit adverse effects, including bone loss.
therapies_index.administration: Various add-back regimens are described, without a general dosing schedule.

therapies_index.name: tibolone
approved_indications: Mentioned among add-back treatments reported with GnRH agonists.

therapies_index.name: testosterone
approved_indications: Mentioned among add-back treatments reported with GnRH agonists.

therapies_index.name: aromatase inhibitors
approved_indications: Recommended only for endometriosis-associated pain refractory to other medical or surgical options; the guideline states they are not currently licensed for this indication.
therapies_index.administration: May be prescribed with oral contraceptives, progestogens, GnRH agonists or GnRH antagonists.

therapies_index.name: hormonal suppression therapy
therapies_index.mechanism: Hormonal treatments used for endometriosis suppress ovulation.
approved_indications: Should be considered after endometriosis surgery when the woman does not plan to conceive immediately, to prolong pain reduction; it should not be prescribed for women with endometriosis and infertility who are trying to conceive.

therapies_index.name: continuous oestrogen-progestogen regimen
approved_indications: Recommended when MHT is required in women with a history of endometriosis.
therapies_index.administration: Continuous regimen; no dose or route is specified.

therapies_index.name: MHT
approved_indications: May be required after early menopause in a woman with a history of endometriosis; the guideline advises a continuous oestrogen-progestogen regimen if it is needed.
key_toxicities: A systematic review cited by the guideline found a small association between MHT and recurrence of endometriosis.

therapies_index.name: operative laparoscopy
approved_indications: Offered for infertility with stage I-II endometriosis to improve the chance of ongoing clinical pregnancy; may be considered for endometrioma with infertility to improve the chance of spontaneous pregnancy, or for symptomatic deeply infiltrative endometriosis with infertility according to pain and patient preference.
therapies_index.administration: Surgical decision-making takes account of fertility factors, symptoms, prior surgery and the woman's preferences.

therapies_index.name: laparoscopy
approved_indications: May be considered when suspected endometriosis symptoms persist and empirical treatment is ineffective or inappropriate, even with negative imaging; also provides an opportunity to treat lesions.
therapies_index.administration: A gynaecologist with appropriate laparoscopic training should examine the pelvis and abdomen thoroughly. Suspected lesions should be biopsied for histological confirmation.

therapies_index.name: excision
approved_indications: May be considered instead of ablation when operating for endometriosis-associated pain; removed tissue can undergo histopathological examination.
therapies_index.administration: Laparoscopic surgery is preferred to laparotomy unless contraindicated.

therapies_index.name: ablation
approved_indications: Described as a method of removing endometriotic lesions during surgery; the guideline suggests clinicians may consider excision instead for pain.

therapies_index.name: diathermy
approved_indications: Described as a surgical method for eliminating endometriotic lesions and as a haemostasis method during endometrioma cystectomy.
key_toxicities: Non-thermal haemostasis methods were more favourable than diathermy according to postoperative AMH levels in the cited meta-analyses.

therapies_index.name: division of adhesions
approved_indications: Used during endometriosis surgery to restore anatomy.

therapies_index.name: ovarian cystectomy
approved_indications: Recommended as an option instead of drainage and coagulation for ovarian endometrioma to reduce recurrence and pain; may be considered for endometrioma-associated infertility, accounting for ovarian reserve and other fertility factors.
therapies_index.administration: The cyst is excised. Particular caution is advised for recurrent or bilateral endometriomas and when ovarian reserve is a concern.
key_toxicities: The guideline reports a 2.4% risk of ovarian failure after surgery for bilateral endometriomata.

therapies_index.name: CO2 laser vaporisation
approved_indications: Recommended as an option instead of drainage and coagulation for ovarian endometrioma to reduce recurrence and endometriosis-associated pain.
therapies_index.administration: Care is advised to minimise ovarian damage.
key_toxicities: Potential ovarian damage during endometrioma surgery

therapies_index.name: drainage and coagulation
therapies_index.administration: Described as an endometrioma treatment comparator; cystectomy or CO2 laser vaporisation is recommended instead.
key_toxicities: Higher recurrence of endometrioma and associated pain relative to the recommended surgical options

therapies_index.name: drainage and use of oxidised regenerated cellulose
approved_indications: Described as an endometrioma surgical technique.

therapies_index.name: suture
approved_indications: Described as a non-thermal haemostasis method during endometrioma cystectomy.

therapies_index.name: haemostatic agents
approved_indications: Described as non-thermal haemostasis during endometrioma cystectomy.

therapies_index.name: pre-operative freezing of oocytes
approved_indications: Its possibility should be discussed before surgery for bilateral endometriomas.
therapies_index.administration: Before endometrioma surgery.

therapies_index.name: surgical removal of deeply infiltrative endometriosis
approved_indications: May reduce endometriosis-associated pain and improve quality of life.
therapies_index.administration: Should be undertaken by a surgeon experienced in deep disease, preferably through a minimally invasive multidisciplinary approach aiming to remove all lesions.
key_toxicities: Surgical complications, particularly when bowel or urinary structures are involved

therapies_index.name: superficial shaving
approved_indications: Described as an approach to removing colorectal deep endometriosis nodules.
therapies_index.administration: Bowel surgery.

therapies_index.name: discoid resection
approved_indications: Described as an approach to removing colorectal deep endometriosis nodules.
therapies_index.administration: Bowel surgery.

therapies_index.name: segmental resection
approved_indications: Described as an approach to removing deep endometriosis nodules from the bowel.
therapies_index.administration: Segmental bowel resection.

therapies_index.name: excision of the lesion and primary closure of the bladder wall
approved_indications: Described as the usual surgical treatment for bladder endometriosis.
therapies_index.administration: Bladder lesion excision followed by primary closure.

therapies_index.name: ureterolysis
approved_indications: Reported as a surgical treatment in a review of ureteric endometriosis.

therapies_index.name: ureteral resection and re-anastomosis
approved_indications: Reported as a surgical treatment in a review of ureteric endometriosis.

therapies_index.name: ureteroneocystostomy
approved_indications: Reported as a surgical treatment in a review of ureteric endometriosis.

therapies_index.name: hysterectomy
approved_indications: May be considered, with or without oophorectomy, for women who do not intend to conceive and whose conservative treatment has failed; it does not always resolve endometriosis symptoms.
therapies_index.administration: The guideline recommends total rather than sub-total hysterectomy and advises excision of all visible endometriosis lesions.
key_toxicities: When ovaries are conserved, increased risk of recurrent pain and further surgery is reported.

therapies_index.name: oophorectomy
approved_indications: May be considered in conjunction with hysterectomy for selected women with endometriosis.
therapies_index.administration: Consequences of early menopause and a possible need for MHT should be discussed.
key_toxicities: Potential long-term effects of ovary removal

therapies_index.name: salpingectomy
approved_indications: A cited review found moderate-quality evidence that salpingectomy for tubal disease before ART probably increases pregnancy rates.
therapies_index.administration: Before ART in the setting of tubal disease.

therapies_index.name: tubal occlusion
approved_indications: A cited review found that it may increase pregnancy rates before ART, although the evidence was of low quality.
therapies_index.administration: Before ART in the setting of tubal disease.

therapies_index.name: IUI
approved_indications: IUI with ovarian stimulation should be considered for infertility with stage I-II endometriosis; the guideline also says IUI could be considered for stage III-IV disease with patent tubes, but evidence is limited.
therapies_index.administration: May be particularly effective within six months after surgery for stage I-II endometriosis.

therapies_index.name: IUI with ovarian stimulation
approved_indications: Should be considered for management of infertility with stage I-II endometriosis.
therapies_index.administration: Intrauterine insemination combined with ovarian stimulation.

therapies_index.name: ART
approved_indications: Recommended for endometriosis-associated infertility, particularly with impaired tubal function or coexisting male-factor infertility.
therapies_index.administration: The guideline uses this term for interventions that handle embryos or oocytes; in vitro fertilisation and ICSI are included.

therapies_index.name: IVF
approved_indications: Listed among ART options for endometriosis-associated infertility.

therapies_index.name: ICSI
approved_indications: Listed among ART options for endometriosis-associated infertility.

therapies_index.name: acupuncture
therapies_index.administration: May be discussed as a complementary strategy; the guideline cannot recommend it individually to treat endometriosis-related symptoms.

therapies_index.name: physiotherapy
therapies_index.administration: May be discussed to address quality of life and psychological well-being; the guideline cannot recommend an individual physiotherapy intervention for endometriosis-related symptoms.

therapies_index.name: trigger point manual therapy
therapies_index.administration: A cited review did not recommend it for chronic pain after included trials showed no significant pain reduction compared with general massage.

therapies_index.name: electrotherapy
therapies_index.administration: May be discussed with women, but the guideline cannot recommend it individually for endometriosis-related symptoms because of limitations in the evidence.

therapies_index.name: Transcutaneous Electrical Nerve Stimulation (TENS)
therapies_index.administration: Mentioned as the subject of an endometriosis-related pain study that was subsequently retracted.

therapies_index.name: neuromuscular electrical stimulation
therapies_index.administration: Used for 10 weeks in a cited retrospective study; the guideline makes no individual recommendation for electrotherapy.

therapies_index.name: high-intensity laser therapy
therapies_index.administration: Investigated over 8 weeks alongside hormonal treatment in a cited small trial; the guideline makes no individual recommendation for electrotherapy.

therapies_index.name: psychological interventions
therapies_index.administration: May be discussed to address quality of life and psychological well-being, but the guideline cannot recommend an individual intervention for endometriosis-related symptoms.

therapies_index.name: support-expressive psychotherapeutic interventions
approved_indications: A cited narrative review suggested that women with endometriosis may benefit; this is not an individual recommendation of the guideline.
therapies_index.administration: Individual or group setting was described by the cited review.

therapies_index.name: nutrition
therapies_index.administration: Dietary strategies may be discussed, but the guideline cannot recommend an individual nutritional intervention for endometriosis-related symptoms.

therapies_index.name: traditional Chinese medicine
therapies_index.administration: May be discussed as a non-medical strategy; the guideline cannot recommend it individually for endometriosis-related symptoms.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Women with suspected endometriosis, including those awaiting imaging, surgery or histological confirmation.
decision_rules: Discuss and offer empirical medical treatment when symptoms and examination support a presumptive diagnosis; do not delay treatment solely to obtain diagnostic confirmation.
Choose treatment jointly with the woman, considering plans to conceive, previous treatment, adverse effects, cost and availability.

Refer to a Gynaecologist if symptoms are severe, persistent or recurrent; examination shows endometriosis; infertility is present; initial treatment is ineffective, intolerable or contraindicated; or imaging suggests more extensive or deeply infiltrative disease.
Refer suspected or confirmed deeply infiltrative endometriosis involving the bowel, bladder or ureter to a specialist endometriosis service.

recommended_regimens.name: empiric medical treatment
recommended_regimens.summary: Offer an opportunity to begin medical symptom management on the basis of a presumptive diagnosis; this may improve quality of life.

alternative_regimens.name: laparoscopy
alternative_regimens.summary: Consider surgical assessment as another viable approach to symptoms; neither laparoscopy nor empirical medical treatment has been shown to be superior.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Consider when empirical treatment is ineffective or inappropriate, including when a woman is trying to conceive or cannot tolerate medical treatment, even if imaging is negative.

not_recommended.name: pregnancy for management of endometriosis symptoms
not_recommended.reason: Pregnancy has not been shown to cure endometriosis, so women should not be advised to conceive for this purpose.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Treatment need not be started when endometriosis is asymptomatic.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Women with endometriosis-associated pain, including cyclical or menstrual pain.
decision_rules: Offer analgesia for pain, either alone or alongside hormonal suppression; analgesics may also address breakthrough pain.
Refer severe pain that does not respond to first-line analgesia and hormonal suppression to a pain specialist.

recommended_regimens.name: paracetamol
recommended_regimens.summary: Offer as an analgesic option, alone or with NSAIDs; it does not change the pathological course of endometriosis.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: A systematic review found that paracetamol was not more effective than placebo for pain reduction; the underlying evidence was described as very low quality.

recommended_regimens.name: NSAIDs
recommended_regimens.summary: Offer for pain, alone or together with paracetamol, while accounting for gastrointestinal effects and possible kidney injury with long-term use.

recommended_regimens.name: neuromodulator therapies
recommended_regimens.summary: May be used for endometriosis-associated pain, generally within a broader strategy coordinated with a specialist pain management service. Discussed examples are amitriptyline, nortriptyline, duloxetine, gabapentin and pregabalin.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: In RCTs concerning chronic pelvic pain, neuromodulators were not shown to be clearly superior to placebo.

not_recommended.name: opioid medication
not_recommended.reason: Its use for endometriosis-associated pain is not recommended because of adverse effects and the potential for dependence.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Evidence for analgesics specifically in endometriosis is limited. Neuromodulators can cause severe, dose-limiting adverse effects.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Women seeking medical treatment for endometriosis-associated pain.
decision_rules: Offer combined hormonal contraception or progestogens as first-line hormonal treatment.
Agree on treatment with the woman after considering pregnancy intentions, preferences, prior hormonal treatment, adverse effects, individual efficacy, cost and availability.
Recommend continuous rather than cyclic use when prescribing combined oral contraceptive medication.

recommended_regimens.name: combined hormonal contraception
recommended_regimens.summary: First-line hormonal option for pain, available as an oral pill, vaginal ring or transdermal patch.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: Systematic reviews cited by the guideline reported statistically significant reductions in endometriosis-related pain and improvement in quality of life; another review found clinically and statistically significant reductions in dysmenorrhea, non-cyclical pelvic pain and dyspareunia.

recommended_regimens.name: COCP
recommended_regimens.summary: Use the combined oral contraceptive option continuously for endometriosis-associated pain.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: A systematic review and meta-analysis comparing continuous with cyclic OCP use reported less dysmenorrhea recurrence with the continuous regimen (RR 0.24; 95%CI 0.06-0.91).

recommended_regimens.name: progestogens
recommended_regimens.summary: First-line hormonal option that can be offered as an oral pill, levonorgestrel intra-uterine system, etonogestrel-releasing subdermal implant or medroxyprogesterone acetate depot intramuscular injection.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: An RCT comparing the etonogestrel-releasing subdermal implant with the LNG-releasing IUS found significant reductions in pain scores with both.

not_recommended.name: danazol
not_recommended.reason: It is no longer recommended, principally because of severe adverse effects when other medical options have equivalent efficacy.

response_assessment.method: Assess whether initial hormonal treatment is effective, tolerated or contraindicated.
response_assessment.interpretation: The guideline identifies women whose initial hormonal treatment is ineffective after six months, intolerable or contraindicated as an audit group requiring an established gynaecology referral pathway.

supportive_care: Discuss the potential for acne, oedema, weight gain, irregular bleeding and breast tenderness with progestogens.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Hormonal treatment is unsuitable while a woman is trying to conceive because it suppresses ovulation. Individual non-medical interventions cannot be recommended on the available evidence, but clinicians may discuss traditional Chinese medicine, nutrition, electrotherapy, acupuncture, physiotherapy and psychological interventions to address quality of life and psychological well-being.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Women requiring second-line hormonal treatment for endometriosis-associated pain.
decision_rules: Offer GnRH agonists or antagonists with add-back hormone replacement therapy as second-line treatment.
Reserve GnRH agonists for second-line use because of their adverse-effect profile and the lack of consensus on dose and duration.
Reserve GnRH antagonists for second-line use because dose and duration lack consensus.

recommended_regimens.name: GnRH agonists
recommended_regimens.summary: Offer with add-back hormonal treatment to mitigate hot flushes, vaginal dryness, loss of bone mineral density and other induced menopausal symptoms. Examples discussed are triptorelin, leuprorelin and goserelin.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: A Cochrane review found GnRH agonists more effective than placebo for endometriosis-related pain but less effective than LNG-IUS and oral danazol; these comparisons do not constitute recommendations to use danazol.
recommended_regimens.duration_cycles: The guideline does not establish a specific dose or treatment duration.

recommended_regimens.name: GnRH antagonists
recommended_regimens.summary: Offer with add-back hormone replacement therapy. The discussed agents include elagolix, linzagolix and relugolix.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: Two placebo-controlled trials found elagolix significantly superior to placebo for reducing endometriosis-related pain.
recommended_regimens.duration_cycles: The guideline does not establish a class-wide dose or treatment duration.

recommended_regimens.name: relugolix
recommended_regimens.summary: The combination formulation available in Ireland contains 40 mg relugolix/1 mg estradiol hemihydrate/0.5 mg norethisterone and is taken as a daily tablet. It is licensed for endometriosis but was not reimbursed by the HSE at guideline publication.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: In the SPIRIT 1 and 2 trials, dysmenorrhoea improvement with combination relugolix + HRT versus placebo was SPIRIT 1: 75% versus 27%; SPIRIT 2, 75% versus 30%. For noncyclical pelvic pain, the respective comparisons were 59% versus 40%, and 66% versus 43%. After 24 weeks of combination therapy, mean bone mineral density reduction was less that 1% and was not considered clinically significant.
recommended_regimens.duration_cycles: Daily tablet; the guideline does not specify an overall treatment duration.

response_assessment.method: Bone densitometry imaging for the relugolix combination formulation.
response_assessment.interpretation: Further bone densitometry is recommended as considered appropriate thereafter.

supportive_care: Provide add-back hormone replacement therapy with GnRH agonists or antagonists.
Use nonhormonal contraception for at least the first month of treatment with the relugolix combination formulation.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Evidence directly comparing GnRH agonists with antagonists is scarce. In SPIRIT 1 and 2, delaying HRT until after 12 weeks of relugolix monotherapy did not improve efficacy and was associated with more hot flushes and substantial bone density reduction.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Women whose endometriosis-related pain remains refractory after other medical or surgical options.
decision_rules: Recommend aromatase inhibitors only once other medical and surgical treatment options have been exhausted.
They can be prescribed alongside oral contraceptives, progestogens, GnRH agonists or GnRH antagonists.

recommended_regimens.name: aromatase inhibitors
recommended_regimens.summary: Reserve this option for refractory pain. The guideline discusses anastrozole and letrozole; aromatase inhibitors are not currently licensed for endometriosis-related pain.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: The guideline describes moderate-level RCT evidence of reduced pain scores, particularly when pain has resisted earlier medical or surgical treatment.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Long-term effects have not been established. Reported serious adverse effects include vaginal dryness, hot flushes and diminished bone mineral density.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Women following surgery for endometriosis who do not plan to conceive immediately.
decision_rules: Consider postoperative hormonal suppression to prolong pain reduction and potentially reduce disease recurrence.
Do not apply this postoperative suppression pathway to women attempting immediate conception.

recommended_regimens.name: hormonal suppression treatment
recommended_regimens.summary: Consider after endometriosis surgery if pregnancy is not immediately planned.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: Reviews cited by the guideline suggested that postoperative hormone therapy may reduce disease recurrence compared with surgery alone.

recommended_regimens.name: combined hormonal contraception
recommended_regimens.summary: A first-line medical option to extend the reduction in postoperative endometriosis-related pain; available as an oral pill, vaginal ring or transdermal patch.

recommended_regimens.name: progestogens
recommended_regimens.summary: A first-line medical option to extend postoperative pain reduction, available as an oral pill, levonorgestrel intrauterine system, etonogestrel-releasing implant or medroxyprogesterone acetate depot injection.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: A review specifically examining LNG-IUS for symptomatic recurrence after surgery found no high-quality evidence supporting that practice. The guideline reports that symptoms recur in 40-45% of women after surgery and that up to 30% undergo another endometriosis operation within five years of their first.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Women considering surgery as an option for endometriosis-associated pain.
decision_rules: Offer surgery among the options for pain reduction; decide jointly whether hormonal or surgical treatment better fits the woman's preferences and circumstances.
Discuss the operation, expected effect on symptoms, risks, benefits and possible need for further surgery before proceeding.
Use laparoscopy rather than laparotomy unless contraindicated.
When operating, clinicians may consider excision in preference to ablation.

recommended_regimens.name: surgery
recommended_regimens.summary: Offer surgical treatment as one option for pain. Techniques discussed include excision, diathermy or ablation of lesions and division of adhesions.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: The guideline reports lower pain scores at six months postoperatively with surgical treatment than with diagnostic laparoscopy alone.

recommended_regimens.name: excision
recommended_regimens.summary: Clinicians may consider excising endometriosis rather than ablating it when surgery is undertaken for pain; excision also allows histopathological assessment.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: Pundir et al., 2017 found significantly greater reductions in pain scores, dyschezia and chronic pelvic pain with excision than with ablation; reductions in dysmenorrhoea and dyspareunia were not statistically significant. A later review by Burks et al. found no significant difference in pain scores at 12 months post-operatively.

alternative_regimens.name: ablation
alternative_regimens.summary: A surgical technique for eliminating lesions, although the committee favours excision where possible.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Consider within an individual surgical plan; the effectiveness of ablation for deeply infiltrative disease is unclear.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Long-term comparative surgical outcomes are limited, and the reviewed evidence spans superficial through deep disease.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Women with an ovarian endometrioma and pain symptoms for whom surgery is being considered.
decision_rules: Anticipate additional endometriosis, including deeply infiltrative endometriosis, during surgery.
Use cystectomy or CO2 laser vaporisation rather than drainage and coagulation to reduce endometrioma recurrence and associated pain.
Minimise ovarian damage, particularly when operating on a recurrent endometrioma or when ovarian reserve is a concern.
Discuss the possibility of pre-operative oocyte freezing in particular when endometriomas are bilateral.

recommended_regimens.name: cystectomy
recommended_regimens.summary: Surgical option for an ovarian endometrioma with pain, preferred over drainage and coagulation; counsel about reduced ovarian reserve and possible loss of the ovary.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: A Cochrane review of endometriomas 3 cm or larger associated cystectomy with fewer cyst recurrences, less recurrence of non-menstrual pain and less further surgery than drainage with bipolar coagulation.

recommended_regimens.name: CO2 laser vaporisation
recommended_regimens.summary: Surgical option preferred over drainage and coagulation for reducing endometrioma recurrence and associated pain.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: A retrospective study of n=125 women found similar cyst recurrence rates following cystectomy and laser vaporisation.

not_recommended.name: drainage and coagulation
not_recommended.reason: Cystectomy or CO2 laser vaporisation is preferred because these options can reduce endometrioma recurrence and endometriosis-associated pain.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The guideline reports a 2.4% risk of ovarian failure following surgery for bilateral endometriomata. Reviewed haemostasis studies favoured non-thermal methods over diathermy according to postoperative AMH levels.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Women with deeply infiltrative endometriosis and pain, particularly where the bowel, bladder or ureter is involved.
decision_rules: Consider surgical removal because it may lessen pain and improve quality of life.
Have surgery performed by a surgeon experienced in deep endometriosis, preferably using a minimally invasive approach in a multidisciplinary setting with the aim of removing all lesions.
Agree on surgery after discussing anticipated outcomes, benefits and risks with the woman.

recommended_regimens.name: surgical removal of deeply infiltrative endometriosis
recommended_regimens.summary: May reduce endometriosis-associated pain and improve quality of life.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: In a study of almost 5000 women undergoing laparoscopic excision of rectovaginal endometriosis, reductions in several pain symptoms persisted at two years. The overall incidence of complications was 6.8%; major gastrointestinal complications occurred in 1.1% of operations and urinary-tract complications in 1% of procedures.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: For colorectal disease, described approaches are superficial shaving, discoid resection and segmental bowel resection. Bladder lesions are usually excised with primary bladder-wall closure. Ureteric lesions may be excised after stenting; intrinsic lesions or significant obstruction may require segmental excision with end-to-end anastomosis or reimplantation. A cited report associates bowel endometriosis surgery with postoperative complications of up to 13.9%.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Women who do not plan to conceive and whose conservative treatment has not succeeded.
decision_rules: Consider hysterectomy with or without oophorectomy, but explain that symptoms will not invariably resolve.
Perform total rather than sub-total hysterectomy if proceeding.
Excise all visible endometriosis lesions during hysterectomy.
If considering oophorectomy, discuss early menopause and the possible need for MHT.

recommended_regimens.name: hysterectomy
recommended_regimens.summary: Consider with or without oophorectomy after unsuccessful conservative treatment in women not planning pregnancy; it is not guaranteed to relieve endometriosis symptoms.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: The guideline cites a 6-fold risk of recurrent pain and an 8.1-times greater risk of reoperation after hysterectomy with ovarian conservation.

recommended_regimens.name: total hysterectomy
recommended_regimens.summary: Use in preference to sub-total hysterectomy because retaining the cervix may leave endometriosis within or adjacent to it.

alternative_regimens.name: oophorectomy
